summary: Iteration 2 — revision pass on the uncommitted /dashboard skeleton-flash change, addressing all three qa-acceptance findings from the 2026-09-20T142500Z loop-back. (1) HIGH, back/forward staleness: DashboardBody's client fetch is no longer suppressed by `initialData !== null`. The effect now runs on every mount (deps [authLoading, user, token, fetchDashboard]) — exactly the pre-server-render semantics — while the FetchState seed from `initialData` is kept, so the first paint is still real content and AC-1 does not regress. The fetch is silent when data is already present: it never renders a loading state (fetchDashboard only ever sets success or error, never loading) and a failed background revalidation no longer clobbers painted content — new helper `errorUnlessAlreadyLoaded(message)` returns a functional updater that keeps `prev` when `prev.status === 'success'`, so only a user with no content ever sees the error card. VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY, not theoretically, two ways. (a) Live browser repro using qa-acceptance's own probe method, extended with a control: three throwaway routes (probea = dynamic server component via cookies() passing a `srv-<Date.now()>` payload to TWO client components rendered side by side — ProbeFixed with the new unconditional-revalidate logic and ProbeGuarded with iteration-1's `initialData !== null` guard — plus probeb and a /api/probe route returning `api-<Date.now()>` after a 700ms delay so the intermediate render is observable), `pnpm build && PORT=3123 pnpm start` on this app's real production config, driven by Playwright/Chromium (/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194) through visit probea -> click next/link to probeb -> wait 1500ms (>> staleTimes.dynamic=0) -> browser Back. Results: the restored page's `data-seeded` attribute was byte-identical to the first visit's (srv-1789914822808) and the document identity marker survived, confirming Next restored the cached RSC segment with NO fresh server render — qa's precondition reproduces on this build. ProbeGuarded (iteration-1 logic) still showed srv-1789914822808 two seconds after Back — the reported defect reproduces exactly. ProbeFixed painted the stale seeded value immediately on restore (never 'LOADING', i.e. no skeleton flash) and then self-corrected to a brand-new api-1789914826500, distinct from both the seeded value and the first visit's fetch. All six probe assertions passed; every probe file and the driver script were deleted afterwards (git status clean). (b) New DOM-level test app/tests/components/dashboardBodyRevalidate.test.tsx (happy-dom, createRoot + act, following tests/hooks/useMatchmakingQueue.test.ts's established pattern) mounts the REAL DashboardBody and asserts: with non-null initialData it still calls /api/dashboard exactly once, keeps showing the seeded 3-1 record with no SkeletonCard and no spinner while that fetch is in flight, then shows 4-1 once it resolves and does NOT re-arm the effect (one fetch per mount); a rejected background fetch leaves the 3-1 content with no role=alert; and the initialData===null path still surfaces the error card. Both new tests were PROVEN TO FAIL against the old behaviour (re-adding the `initialData !== null` guard fails test 1; reverting errorUnlessAlreadyLoaded to an unconditional error set fails test 2) before being restored byte-identical to the verified version. (2) MEDIUM, type drift: new app/src/db/dashboard.ts owns `DashboardData` and exports `buildDashboardPayload(uid, email): Promise<DashboardData>` (same five reads, same per-read .catch() fallbacks, same duelStats narrowing as before). Both producers now call it — page.tsx assigns its result to `DashboardData | null`, and route.ts returns `NextResponse.json(payload)` where payload is typed, so tsc now checks the API response against the same interface instead of an untyped literal. DashboardBody re-exports the type (`export type { DashboardData } from '../../src/db/dashboard'`) so existing imports, including verifier's test, are unchanged. Placement follows the src/db/settings.ts + getUserSettings precedent (type owned by the db module, client imports it). The type-only imports of the four component interfaces into the db module and of DashboardData into the client component are fully erased — grepped the production client chunks for buildDashboardPayload / getUserFreeClimbRecord / beta_waitlist_joined_at from my module: absent. (The pre-existing PrismaClient text in two client chunks is present in the baseline HEAD build too — not introduced here.) DELTA TO NOTE FOR REVIEW: making route.ts return the shared builder's value means its duelStats is now the same four counters page.tsx already sent (wins, losses, current_streak, best_streak) instead of the raw Prisma row, which also carried unused user_id and updated_at. That is the unavoidable consequence of type-checking the route against DashboardData, and is invisible to every consumer — DashboardBody types the response as DashboardData, and the only other consumer, app/mobile/src/contexts/AppDataContext.tsx, declares its own DashboardData with just user + freeClimb. No status codes, error envelope, auth, logging, or field names changed. (3) LOW, BetaBanner layout shift: the beta block is now decided entirely by server-known `betaJoined` — `betaJoined ? <badge> : <BetaBanner token={token} />` with the `token &&` gate removed, so whichever element will show is present in the first server-rendered frame and nothing pops in later. BetaBanner's prop became `token: string | null` (it is used only here) with `if (!token) return;` in handleSubmit and `disabled={state === 'loading' || token === null}` on the Join button, so only that one action waits for the Firebase session — the banner's layout box does not. Rendering mode re-verified by the established detached-worktree method: `git worktree add --detach HEAD`, symlinked node_modules, clean `rm -rf .next && pnpm build` in both trees, route tables normalised and diffed — exactly one of 125 lines differs (`○ /dashboard` at HEAD vs `ƒ /dashboard` now), nothing else moved; prerender-manifest.json agrees (/dashboard present in the baseline's static routes, absent in the modified build). Worktree removed, next-env.d.ts churn reverted, no AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md left behind. All six context/gates.json gates green (app 82 files / 751 tests). No new dependencies. requireAuth.ts, firebaseAdmin.ts and authCookie.ts untouched; route.ts changed only by the authorised shared-builder refactor. Working tree left uncommitted.
goal: Fix the three qa-acceptance findings on the uncommitted /dashboard change — the HIGH back/forward staleness regression, the MEDIUM DashboardData type-drift risk, and the LOW BetaBanner layout shift — without regressing AC-1..AC-5, and prove the staleness fix against a real back-navigation browser repro.

feedbackAddressed.issue: Back/forward navigation restores a stale server-resolved initialData with no self-heal, because the client fetch effect permanently early-returns on initialData !== null.
feedbackAddressed.resolution: Client fetch is now an unconditional post-mount background revalidation (seed kept for zero-flash first paint; silent in flight; failures no longer clobber painted content). Proven fixed by a live Playwright back-navigation repro that includes an iteration-1 control which still reproduces the defect, plus a DOM-level test of the real component that fails against the old guard.

feedbackAddressed.issue: Two DashboardData producers; route.ts built an untyped literal and could silently diverge.
feedbackAddressed.resolution: Extracted src/db/dashboard.ts::buildDashboardPayload(uid, email): Promise<DashboardData>, called from both page.tsx and route.ts; the route's response is now type-checked against the shared interface. Behaviour unchanged apart from duelStats carrying only the four counters both sides already used (see summary delta note).

feedbackAddressed.issue: BetaBanner mounted on client-only `token`, appearing ~100-500ms late and shifting the cards below it.
feedbackAddressed.resolution: Both beta branches are now driven by server-known betaJoined; BetaBanner takes `token: string | null` and disables only its Join button until the Firebase session resolves.

gatesRun.name: back-navigation browser probe (throwaway, deleted)
gatesRun.command: pnpm build && PORT=3123 pnpm start + Playwright/Chromium visit→link→wait 1.5s→Back
gatesRun.result: pass — 6/6 assertions: stale RSC segment restored, no LOADING flash on restore, fixed component self-healed to a fresh value, iteration-1 control stayed stale

learnings.insight: qa-acceptance's throwaway-probe method gets materially stronger when the probe page renders BOTH the proposed fix and the current (defective) logic side by side, fed by the same server prop, so one Back covers both. That turns 'the fix appears to work' into a controlled comparison: in this run the iteration-1 control still showed the stale srv- value 2s after Back while the fixed component healed to a fresh api- value, which simultaneously proves the probe faithfully reproduces the reported defect and that the effect change (not some unrelated build difference) is what fixes it. Adding a slow (700ms) probe API also makes the intermediate 'seeded but not yet revalidated' frame deterministically observable, so 'no loading flash on restore' becomes an assertion rather than a race.
learnings.action: When empirically validating a fix for a router/cache behaviour, render the before-logic and after-logic side by side in the same probe page and assert both outcomes, and slow the probe endpoint enough that the in-flight frame is observable instead of racing the driver.

learnings.insight: Mounting a component whose effect depends on useRouter()/useAuth() values with a mock that returns a FRESH object per call produces an infinite refetch loop in the test (the effect re-arms on every state change), which surfaces as an opaque 'Test timed out in 5000ms' rather than a failed assertion. Hit while writing the DashboardBody revalidation test: the real useRouter and the memoised AuthContext value are both stable, so this was a harness artifact, not a production defect — but it is indistinguishable from a real runaway-refetch bug until you log the fetch URLs. Also worth knowing: mounting DashboardBody drags in Navbar and WalletCard, which fetch /api/notifications/count, /api/settings and /api/wallet, so a blanket fetch mock must route by URL (or leave the others pending) or unrelated components crash on the wrong response shape.
learnings.action: In component mount tests, return one stable object from useRouter/useAuth mocks (defined outside the factory) and route the fetch stub by URL. If a mount test times out rather than failing an assertion, log the fetch URLs first — a repeating endpoint means the effect is re-arming on mock identity, not a hung promise.

learnings.insight: Collapsing two producers of the same payload into one typed builder has a shape side effect that is easy to mis-read as an unauthorised behaviour change: the API route previously emitted the raw Prisma duel-stats row (extra user_id, updated_at), and returning the shared DashboardData-typed value necessarily drops those. Checked every consumer before doing it — the web client types the response as DashboardData, and app/mobile/src/contexts/AppDataContext.tsx declares its own narrower DashboardData with only user + freeClimb — so nothing reads the dropped fields. Type-only imports across the client/server boundary (component interfaces into src/db, DashboardData into a 'use client' file) are erased: verified by grepping the production client chunks for the db module's identifiers, and by confirming the pre-existing PrismaClient text in two client chunks is equally present in the baseline HEAD build.
learnings.action: When reviewing a de-duplication refactor of an API payload, check the consumer list for the dropped fields rather than treating any response-shape delta as a violation — and verify client/server type-only imports by grepping .next/static for the server module's identifiers, comparing against a baseline build before attributing a bundle hit to the change.

learnings.insight: The 'server-resolves payload -> client seeds from initialData' pattern (settings/SettingsForm, now /dashboard) needs three properties to be safe, not just the seed: (a) the client fetch must still run on every mount so a bfcache/history-traversal-restored instance self-heals, (b) that fetch must never render a loading state when data is already seeded, and (c) a failed background revalidation must keep the painted content rather than replacing it with an error card — a functional state updater that returns `prev` when prev is already success is the smallest way to express (c). /settings still has the permanent seed-and-suppress guard and therefore still carries the back/forward staleness gap; it is lower impact there (settings change only from that page) but it is the same defect class.
learnings.action: Apply all three properties whenever converting a page to server-resolved initialData, and treat the existing /settings guard as a known open instance of the same pattern if its data ever becomes mutable from another flow.
